newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Duma to change Rosgosstrakh sale scheme.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Duma to change Rosgosstrakh sale scheme.

text.p: Russia's State Duma (lower house of parliament) has prepared a resolution appealing to President Boris Yeltsin to draw up a new privatisation plan for Russia's biggest insurer OAO Rosgosstrakh, replacing the current scheme.
"Under the circumstances, Rosgosstrakh privatisation may incur a breach of rights of millions of Russians," the draft document, obtained by Reuters on Thursday, said.
The Duma is to discuss the document on Friday.
Under the current privatisation scheme employees bought 20 percent of Rosgosstrakh shares and a nine-member management team has a priority right to 30 percent.
The remaining 50 percent will be put up for a cash auction this year.

The Duma said Rosgosstrakh had to have a special privatisation scheme, citing the importance of the company, which holds 85 percent of the insurance market for individuals and owes its clients huge amounts.
Rosgosstrakh itself estimates its share of the voluntary insurance market at 17 percent.

According to Duma estimates Rosgosstrakh owes about 30 billion roubles in 1992 prices (about $300 million at early 1992 exchange rates) to its clients in debt accumulated before economic reforms started in 1992.
Rosgosstrakh said its debt amounted to 24 billion roubles in 1992 prices. It also said a presidential decree had converted the debt into state debt and the company was not responsible for it.
The Duma criticised Rosgosstrakh for not including the question of debt repayment in its privatisation scheme.
The Moscow Arbitration Court has suspended Rosgosstrakh's privatisation pending a suit from a union of depositors at state savings bank Sberbank and Rosgosstrakh over the debt.
The court ordered the privatisation to be suspended until its next sitting on March 25.
